Experimental. This package is a personal collection of utility functions that have grown out of day-to-day statistical work: things I kept wishing R had out of the box, patterns I found myself repeating, and new ideas I wanted to try out. Rather than letting them accumulate as loose scripts, I packaged them up properly with the help of Claude Code to get a solid starting point: documentation, tests, and a vignette from the start. Consider it a living experiment.

Related packages

These bodies of work grew large enough to leave and become packages of their own. They are standalone — none of them depends on daos, or daos on them.

Package What it does
taskr (private) Taskwarrior-style task management backed by a shared SQLite file
statbank (private) Client and keyboard browser for the Greenland and Faroese statbanks
cvrr Published Danish annual reports: the CVR distribution service, XBRL, and sign reconciliation
taxmill PDF financial statements milled into a tidy Excel dataset, locally
pathr Frictionless file paths: a file browser, open-in-explorer, and RStudio addins for pasted Windows paths
pnrr Danish CPR numbers: clean, derive birth date, age and sex, diagnose a column, pseudonymise

Installation 

pak::pak("dataniel/daos")

What it looks like

Readers and writers now live in their own package, lazer: read_files(), read_workbook(), inspect_excel(), write_excel(), read_access(), and read_sut(), write_sut() and convert_sut() for Greenlandic supply and use table files (SUT, the TA files) in both layouts.

library(lazer)

panel <- read_files("data/dat{2020:2024}.parquet", names = 2020:2024,
                    out = "bind", .id = "year")

When read_files() warns about type mismatches, something changed upstream, and view_types() in daos shows which column, in which file.

Checkpoints instead of silent assumptions now live in their own package, expectr: expect_empty(), expect_none(), expect_unique(), expect_balanced(), expect_no_overlap() and tally_violations().

library(expectr)

sales |>
  expect_none(is.na(customer_id), abort_msg = "Sales without a customer id") |>
  expect_unique(order_id)

CPR numbers now live in their own package, pnrr: clean_cpr(), add_cpr_info() and age(), plus diagnose_cpr() for what is wrong with a CPR column and pseudo_cpr() for serial numbers in place of the CPR number.

Danish and Greenlandic identifiers, and a file a colleague can read.

companies |>
  dplyr::mutate(cvr = clean_cvr(cvr),                 # strips DK and separators
                branche = format_db07(branche)) |>    # one DB07 format
  lazer::write_excel(f("companies_{nowf()}.xlsx"))

lazer::write_excel() writes an xlsx meant to be opened by a person: bold frozen header, thousand separators, blank cells for NA. f() is glue::glue() under a shorter name, and nowf() is a formatted timestamp.

Functions

Function Description
%??% Null-coalescing operator that returns a default when x is NULL, empty, all-NA, or all-""
%like% Regex matching that preserves NA (unlike grepl)
clean_cvr() Standardise CVR numbers: strip separators and the DK VAT prefix
format_db07() Automatically handle mixed DB07 input; choose dotted (01.11.00) or compact (011100) output
db_label() Look up Danish industry labels with an explicit DB07 or DB25 version
inspect_db() Inspect mixed full DB07/DB25 codes; flag shared codes and show both labels
convert_db07_to_db25() / convert_db25_to_db07() Convert full industry codes using DST’s bundled keys; strict or simplified mapping
drop_empty_rows() Drop rows empty across selected columns; optionally include blank text
drop_empty_cols() Drop entirely empty selected columns
f() String interpolation shorthand (glue::glue alias)
flag_duplicates() Prepend isdup/dupid columns to mark duplicate rows
is_blank() Test whether a value is blank in the broadest sense
nowf() Formatted current timestamp, e.g. for file names
screen_timeseries() Fast interactive time-series screening with optional in-app diagnostics and seasonal plots
diagnose_timeseries() Time-series statistics, seasonal/outlier screening, stationarity and structural breaks, optionally by group
shh() Suppress messages and warnings during evaluation
split_by() Split a data frame into a named list by grouping columns
summon() Retrieve objects matching a regex pattern from an environment
view_types() Compare column types across data frames (or a list from lazer::read_files()) and flag which would break a bind

The readers and writers (read_files(), read_workbook(), inspect_excel(), write_excel(), read_access() and the SUT functions) are in lazer, and the CPR functions in pnrr.
